newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq denies U.S. F-16 attacked its radar.
newsitem.headline: Iraq denies U.S. F-16 attacked its radar.

text.p: Iraqi denied on Sunday a statement from the White House that a U.S. F-16 jet enforcing the no-fly zone in southern Iraq fired a missile at an Iraqi radar installation on Saturday.
"Such American allegations are baseless. No incident of any kind has occurred in Iraq's air space," said the Iraqi news agency, quoting an Iraqi foreign ministry spokesman.
The spokesman said Iraq was still committed to a decision not to fire at U.S. and allied jets patrolling the two no-fly zones in southern and northern Iraq.
The decision was taken in September after a confrontation with the United States because of Baghdad's backing of a Kurdish group in the north against a rival.

"Iraq is still committed to its decision which gives apportunity for political action as a response to a proposal by friendly countries particularly Russia and France to handle the illegal and illegitimate two no-fly zones," the spokesman said.
